Q1: 1-Naphthylamine presents recognized significant hazards for environmental, oral, dermal, eye, and organ/systemic impacts (Tier 1), along with an expanded perspective on potential carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (Tier 2). Endocrine disruption hazards are considered low to moderate (Tier 3), but there is insufficient data to confidently assess inhalation hazards (Tier 4).
Q2: 1-Naphthylamine is identified on California's Proposition 65 list, indicating it is known to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. This classification signifies a notable level of concern, and it is not featured on any lists indicating low hazard.
Q3: 1-Naphthylamine is extensively characterized, with 17,000 literature references, placing it well above the median for the dataset of similar chemicals. Its molecular formula (C10H9N) and 'Small Molecule' classification confirm it is a well-defined chemical, not an undefined or variable substance (i.e., not a UVCB). While its inhalation hazards are currently data deficient (Tier 4), other hazard classes are relatively well-studied.
